claims.text: What the strip looks like Small r, deep S in I and aVL; small q, tall R in II, III and aVF.
claims.quote: rS complexes in leads I and aVL, with small R waves and deep S waves qR complexes in leads II, III and aVF, with small Q waves and tall R waves

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Axis: right axis deviation (+90° to +180°)
I and aVL: small R, deep S (rS complexes)
claims.quote: Small R in I and aVL, small Q in II, III, aVF

claims.text: II, III, aVF: small Q (qR complexes)
claims.quote: Small R in I and aVL, small Q in II, III, aVF
small Q in II, III, aVF QRS < 120 ms Much rarer

claims.text: R-wave peak time in aVF: > 45 ms
claims.quote: R-wave peak time: Time from onset of the QRS to the peak of the R wave in aVF > 45 ms

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Mechanism: impulses reach the LV only via the anterior fascicle
claims.quote: Impulses are conducted to the left ventricle only via the anterior fascicle

claims.text: Spread: the main wave of depolarization then spreads along the free LV wall downward and rightward — tall R waves inferiorly, deep S waves laterally
claims.quote: The major wave of depolarisation then spreads along the free LV wall in a downward and rightward direction, producing tall R waves in inferior leads and deep S waves in the lateral leads.

claims.text: Much rarer than LAFB — the broad posterior fascicle resists damage; it usually occurs with RBBB as a bifascicular block
claims.quote: LPFB is much less common than LAFB, as the broad bundle of fibres that comprise the left posterior fascicle are relatively resistant to damage when compared with the slim single tract that makes up the left anterior fascicle. It is extremely rare to see LPFB in isolation. It usually occurs along with RBBB in the context of a bifascicular block.

claims.text: Diagnose only after excluding other causes of right axis deviation — acute PE, tricyclic overdose, lateral STEMI, RVH
claims.quote: Do not be tempted to diagnose LPFB until you have ruled out more significant causes of right axis deviation: Example: acute pulmonary embolus; tricyclic overdose; lateral STEMI; and right ventricular hypertrophy.

claims.text: Symptoms and treatment Usually no symptoms; no specific treatment is indicated
claims.quote: There are usually no symptoms, but presence of either suggests a heart disorder. Diagnosis is by electrocardiography. No specific treatment is indicated.
